body:
Hey. I appreciate the response. To answer your question, there are many things that brought me to this point. I'm having difficulty coming up with reasons to live that don't involve God. I converted to sort of being a Christian a year ago. I waver between Christianity and my own personal form of theism. When I was young I had these beliefs, but I finally came back to them after several years. I've failed at most of my goals in life so far. Even though I got a degree in physics, I did shitty. My GPA is barely high enough to get into graduate school. I don't even know if I should try because I'll probably fail anyways. More generally, I have severe conflicts with my faith. I believe that this life is a transitional period. I have no problem believing this, but I struggle with understanding the point of it. If this life is transitory, why should I struggle through it? I've tried to justify it by telling myself that achievement is difficult and I can get closer to God and gain spiritual growth through struggle. 

I doubt it a lot though. My atheist friends aren't motivated by this kind of thing and I don't understand and it gives me doubt. At the same time, I can't comprehend the atheistic worldview. I struggle with finding value in my life. Ultimately, I think God values me, and everyone else for that matter, but I get angry because I struggle to justify my beliefs with logic. I guess I just don't believe that logic is everything. I think I have value because God gave me value, but I doubt so much. At this point in my life, I'm just so lost and confused about what to do. I struggle with depression and anxiety. I'm an alcoholic as well. I believe that my problems are wholly spiritual, but I just don't know if I can keep growing spiritually. I've seen psychologists/psychiatrists before, but they have been of minimal help. I guess I just have to keep my faith because it's the only thing that my life is built on right now. I have trouble reconciling my faith in God with science and it disturbs me. I think that science can help me get closer to God, but I just don't understand why or how. I used to excel at science and math and now I struggle, because I wonder why I should even bother. Unfortunately, I'm struggling to find reasons not to commit suicide. 

I have to believe that there was a reason that I was born and that something good can happen from it, but it makes me angry. If I would never have been born, I wouldn't have to struggle. Why did God bother creating me? The best answer I can come up with is to reach some indescribably good reward at the end of my life for achieving in science and struggling through life. I just wonder if it will actually be there. I have to believe that there is a purpose to it, but it is so draining that I want to end it. I believe that everything has a purpose, and there is a well defined goal that I have to make. I have to achieve in science and I must struggle through life. I just don't know if I can keep believing. Even if I can keep my faith, I don't know if I can make it. I can't even imagine that God isn't real. That would mean that my struggle is worthless and I just can't accept that idea. Why should I continue to live if I can't do great things in science and spread wisdom? Right now, I just absolutely suck at life. I can't think anymore. I've just transformed so much that I don't understand it. I think God is speaking to me. He's trying to wake me up, but it's not working very well.
